notes: mean 4.0; weakest is methodological_rigour (3): the locked metric only ever measures routing, so the line's own goal - a better product answer - is never instrumented. evidence_relevance sits at 4 because four of the seven sources are self-published practice evidence, now labelled with an id, an inclusion sentence and a quality note; F1 and F2 were closed after this review, when the INDEX rows were completed and the Patterns bullets sourced. Closing pass, 2026-09-22: all four remaining findings are closed or reframed, each with a reason below, and the grade and the six scores are left as this review set them - methodological_rigour stays at 3 because the reframe of F3 names the unmeasured goal rather than measuring it, which is the honest disposition and still a limitation.

findings.quote: {"note": "03-dora-2025.md", "source": "** DORA, *State of AI-assisted Software Development*, 2025 report, plus the", "class": "grey"
findings.observation: At review time the row was class grey and carried no id, no inclusion and no quality note; four of the seven rows (03 DORA, 04 phuryn, 06 NN/g, 07 playwright/docs) were grey in the same shape. C5, C6, C7 and C13 therefore rested on practice sources whose strength the line never stated, so a reader could not tell how much weight the claim should carry. Closed after this review: all seven rows now carry an id, an inclusion sentence and a verified list, and the four grey rows carry a quality note, so the ungraded-evidence gap no longer holds (the class itself is still practice evidence, which is what keeps evidence_relevance at 4).
findings.fix: Add id, inclusion and a quality/confidence note to every row, or state in the review of each claim that its source is ungraded practice evidence.

findings.quote: Every failure above is a **routing or evidence-class gap**, not a capability gap.
findings.observation: A generalisation across all observed failures with no source, no measurement and no stated refuter; the checker's own warning was that 3 of 3 Patterns bullets name no source, so nothing said what the pattern generalises from and nothing would falsify it. Closed after this review: every bullet now carries the claims it generalises from ([C1], [C2], [C3], [C8], [C13]), so the checker's warning is gone.
findings.fix: Attach each Patterns bullet to the observation it generalises from (a Cnn, a literature/ note or an orx id), or demote it to an open question.

findings.quote: "metric": "number of the eight fixed product prompts that arm the product rule (baseline 0), and whether the shipped skill's scorecard can be applied to a real product question"
findings.observation: The locked metric measures arming and scorecard applicability only. The line's question is whether the structure makes evidence-based product analysis routine, and findings.md leaves "Does a product rule actually improve a product answer? Unmeasured here" as an open question, so the instrument can confirm routing but cannot measure the goal it was locked for.
findings.fix: State in the evaluation that the metric is a routing proxy for the goal, or add the paired run (same prompts with and without the rule, scored against the scorecard) it already names as the missing measurement.
findings.resolution: Reframed on 2026-09-22, not answered, and said so in both places the fix named. evaluation.metric_note in state.json now states that the metric is a routing and applicability proxy that never reads an answer, that the goal measurement was not run, and that metric, baseline and locked_at are unchanged since they were locked. to_human/report.md carries a limits section - 'What this does not show - the headline goal was never measured' - which says the goal was never instrumented (so no null result is being reported either) and names the smallest action that would move it: one paired run on the same prompts with and without the rule, each answer scored blind against the scorecard. Left unrun because it needs model spend and a session on the branch, and this line closed on routing evidence. The dimension stays at 3.

findings.quote: the clean run reports 932 tests OK
findings.observation: The log's final recorded suite result is 932 tests, while findings.md ("Full suite: 931 tests, OK") and to_human/report.md ("931 tests, OK") both record 931. The line's own test-count evidence disagrees with itself, and neither number is re-derived in an artifact here.
findings.fix: Reconcile the count against one run and record the single number in log.md, findings.md and report.md, or mark the count as the value at each run's date.
findings.resolution: Closed on 2026-09-22 by counting, and the counts reconcile as values at two dates. Loading the suite in the tree of 2a5a29e - the commit that landed the change - returns 932 test cases, its parent 2a5a29e^ returns 928, and HEAD today returns 1333; the runner itself was not re-run, since the session runs the suite once. So the log's 932 is the value at the landed revision and the 931 in findings.md and report.md was the first run's, one test below it. All three files now record both numbers with their date and the method, and log.md carries a row for it.

findings.observation: The note is explicit that the five SPACE dimensions were never read (ACM returned 403), so only the abstract is evidence. Yet to_human/report.md names "Forsgren et al., ACM Queue 2021" in the named-standard table for the PE constellation axis; the part used is the abstract's own claim, and the note honestly flags the rest as unread.
findings.fix: Keep the note as is, but make the report's table cite the abstract it actually used, or read the full text before the dimensions are relied on.
findings.resolution: Closed on 2026-09-22 by reading the note and taking the first branch of the fix. The note holds the verbatim abstract, records that ACM Queue and the ACM DL both returned 403 for the full text, and deliberately omits the five dimensions rather than writing them from memory. The report's named-standards row now cites 'the SPACE abstract ... as it is held in literature/02-space-2021-forsgren.md', quotes the abstract's own claim that productivity 'cannot be measured by a single metric or dimension', and states that nothing in the line enumerates the dimensions. The note is left as it stands, and the full text was not fetched.

findings.quote: "falsification": "the consult answer names no recommendation on the class question, or the two models agree on vendoring.", "proof": "to_human/consult-answer.md to_human/report.md"
findings.observation: C10 is marked kind code and supported, but its proof is a transcript of two external models answering a question - an opinion, not a code fact or a line-produced measurement - and C12 depends on C10. Agreement between models is not evidence that the repository should adopt the design.
findings.fix: Reclassify C10 as a decision record rather than a supported code claim, and make any claim that leans on it cite the artifact the decision produced.
findings.resolution: Closed on 2026-09-22 through the CLI, so the write path validated it. C10c supersedes C10 and is the row a reader keeps: it states that the consult is an opinion transcript and not a code fact, that the repository records the user's decision to vendor, and it cites the artifact the decision produced - skills/pm-frameworks/SOURCE, the two vendored bodies and the hash check in tests/test_skills.py - with provenance 'user'. The layer has no 'decision' kind (a proof naming repository artifacts is a code claim), so the reclassification is carried in the statement and the provenance, not in the kind. to_human/report.md's decision section says the same thing, which is what a claim leaning on C10 now cites. The checker still warns that C10 is superseded - a row cannot be repaired in place, and appending is the only write the layer allows.
